description: Cross-language source-NAT POOL ADDRESS grammar parity fixture (#6812 F1 round 3). Every case is decided by BOTH the Rust runtime expander (expand_pool_address in userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs) and the Go shared predicate (sourceNATPoolAddressReason + sourceNATPoolMemberHostCount in pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go); both MUST reach the same accept/reject verdict AND, when accepted, the same expanded host count. A pool member the runtime honors but Go stamps invalid_pool poisons a working pool on the tolerant load / peer-sync path (#1960 no-brick); a member Go admits but the runtime refuses charges the aggregate budget for an allocator that is never built. `hosts` is meaningful only when `ok` is true. This file is the ONE table: neither side keeps a copy, so the two grammars cannot drift apart unnoticed.

cases.note: a canonical ZERO octet is not a leading zero
host bits set: both sides mask to the network base and enumerate the FULL prefix

leading-zero PREFIX LENGTH: netip rejects the non-canonical spelling; ipnet's reader caps the IPv4 field at 2 digits. Same verdict, different reason -- pinned so raising the host cap cannot split them
leading-zero OCTET: the round-3 divergence. ipnet's read_number(10,3,0x100) took this as 10.0.0.0/24 and built a 256-address allocator while Go stamped invalid_pool
4-digit octet: refused by both even before round 3
the BARE branch always refused this -- std rejects a leading-zero octet. Before round 3 the CIDR form of the same address was accepted
leading zeros in a HEXTET are canonical IPv6
v4-mapped: a V6 member on both sides
ipnet's 3-digit IPv6 field ACCEPTS this as /64; the host cap refuses it anyway
leading-zero EMBEDDED v4 octet -- the same round-3 divergence through the v6 path
netip.ParseAddr carries a zone; std::net::IpAddr has no zone model. Go refused this only from round 3 (#5875 caught it one clause later, so the POOL verdict already agreed)
